chosen_line.card: All Streams Flow to the Sea

q1_what_did_you_play: All three one-cost cards, using the full 3 energy. All Streams Flow to the Sea into Sludge Spinner for 9 (it already folds in my 8 Charge), then Water's Edge for 6, then Coral Guard for 5 Block. That is 15 damage onto a 37 HP enemy, leaving it at 22, and I eat 3 of its telegraphed 8 instead of all 8, ending around 45/70. I led with All Streams rather than trailing it because it reads Charge, and I wanted no ordering risk that anything shaved the 8 Charge before it resolved.
q2_other_line_considered: Yes: All Streams Flow to the Sea for 9, then Watatsumi Levy, spending 6 Charge to Muster 2 — which would transform the Water's Edge and Coral Guard still in my hand into random Inazuma Companion cards. That is the only line that uses the 2-cost card at all, since Levy plus anything else does not fit under 3 energy. I rejected it because it trades a known 6 damage and a known 5 Block for two unknown cards drawn from a pool I cannot see, at a point in the fight where nothing is urgent — no lethal in reach, no spike to survive, and Charge already fully cashed into All Streams. Paying 6 Charge on top, when Charge is what makes All Streams a 9 instead of a 5, made the trade worse rather than better.
q3_what_it_gave_up: It gave up the Muster entirely — this hand's only route to the Inazuma Companion cards, and the only play with any upside I cannot enumerate. It also spent the 8 Charge for a flat 9 and banked nothing forward: after this turn my Charge is whatever the resource regenerates, and I have no card-quality improvement to show for the turn. Concretely I chose 15 damage and 5 Block now over 9 damage plus two random cards, i.e. I bought a known tempo turn and sold the fight's variance.
q4_different_intent: Yes. Coral Guard is only worth its energy because an 8-damage attack is telegraphed; against a non-attack intent (a buff, a summon, a debuff) that 5 Block is dead, and with 3 energy the leftover slot cannot buy anything else useful — so I would drop Coral Guard and play All Streams plus Watatsumi Levy, Mustering away the now-dead Coral Guard and the held Water's Edge for two companion cards. A much larger telegraphed hit would not change the line: I would still play exactly what I played, since Coral Guard is already the only mitigation in hand and 5 Block is 5 Block whether the swing is 8 or 20.
